holidays.name: National Macaroon Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy the chewy, sweet, coconut-packed cookie. Whether you like yours dunked in chocolate or plain and golden, this is your excuse to have a few.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance, and its founder isn't clearly known. It joins the many cookie days on the calendar. The treat itself goes back centuries, to almond-based cookies made in European monasteries and bakeries.
holidays.funFact: The coconut macaroon and the French macaron (the pastel sandwich cookie) are different treats. Both descend from the same almond-meringue cookie family, and the name comes from an Italian word for 'paste.'

holidays.name: National Speak in Complete Sentences Day
holidays.description: A gentle nudge to ditch the mumbles, trailing thoughts, and one-word replies. Today you say exactly what you mean, with a subject, a verb, and a satisfying full stop.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with teachers, writers, and grammar fans who want people to slow down and express a whole thought.
holidays.funFact: A complete sentence needs only a subject and a verb. 'Go.' counts, because the subject 'you' is implied. Today's challenge can be very short.

holidays.name: Autonomous Vehicle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate self-driving cars, trucks, and shuttles, and to talk about a future where the vehicle handles the commute while you nap, read, or sing along to the radio.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. Tech enthusiasts and mobility fans use it to spotlight driverless technology and the questions it raises about safety and transportation.
holidays.funFact: Self-driving experiments are older than most people think. Researchers built driverless prototypes in the 1980s, long before today's sensor-covered robotaxis.
